blocks.text: KING OF BABYLON · EXILE & RETURN
Evil-merodach. The king of Babylon who brought Jehoiachin out of prison and fed him at his table.

WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"Evil-merodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison". 2 Kings 25:27
"He spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon". 2 Kings 25:28
Jehoiachin changed his prison garments and ate bread before him "all the days of his life", with a daily allowance from the king. 2 Kings 25:29–30 Jeremiah 52:33–34
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Other captive kings were kept in Babylon with Jehoiachin; Jehoiachin's throne was set above theirs. 2 Kings 25:28
Judah's captive king was given new garments and a place at the king's table. 2 Kings 25:29
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points

SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
"In the year that he began to reign" (2 Kgs 25:27), "in the first year of his reign" (Jer 52:31): the 37th year of Jehoiachin's captivity.
ROGERS (1912)
Ptolemy's canon: two years from 561 BC.

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say why he released Jehoiachin.
Scripture does not call him Nebuchadnezzar's son, and does not say how his reign ended.
Scripture does not say how long Jehoiachin lived after his release.

links.text: Gedaliah, Governor of Judah under Babylon
Belshazzar, King of Babylon, as Daniel calls him
Cyrus, King of Persia, Not given in Scripture. Chronicles and Ezra date his proclamation to "the first year of Cyrus king of Persia"; Daniel mentions his first
Darius the Mede, King over the realm of the Chaldeans (Daniel), Not given. Daniel says he took the kingdom "being about threescore and two years old" and dates
Zerubbabel, Governor of Judah, Not given. Haggai calls him "governor of Judah" in the second year of Darius; he is first among the leaders of the return under C
Josiah, King of Judah, Thirty-one years, from the age of eight (2 Kgs 22:1; 2 Chr 34:1)., c. 641–609 BC, did right in the eyes of the LORD
Jehoahaz, King of Judah, Three months, at the age of twenty-three (2 Kgs 23:31; 2 Chr 36:2)., c. 609 BC, did evil in the eyes of the LORD
